status: filed 2026-11-18 before any run (phase B: the code is commute.rho and run.py); option (b) added at the lead's request before filing
wording: the working definition as stated in theory/2026-11-18_definition_causal_abstraction.md (decisions.md rows 'Working definition of reuse, revised' and 'stated in causal-abstraction terms', 2026-11-18), read as written with the section (c) starred choices; each testable alternative read beside it, one at a time. No verdict on any fine-tune; no cut-off, label or rule added to the definition

level.parts: every MLP neuron (4 x 3072, plus appended ones where a graft adds them), every attention head (4 x 6, plus a grafted seventh), the token embedding, and the unembedding (final norm and lm_head together): every variable on a path from input to output is aligned, so F with every part given M's mechanism is M
level.cells: single units, the identity alignment: a neuron's cell is its c_fc row, its down_proj column and its layer's rms_2; a head's cell is its q, k, v rows, its 128 o_proj columns and its layer's rms_1; the embedding's cell is wte; the unembedding's cell is ln_f and lm_head (tied to wte in the 67M: a fine-tune that moves wte moves both, and both parts are then changed)
level.value of a part: what it writes: a neuron's activation times its output column (a 768-vector); a head's output after o_proj (768); the embedding's row (768); the unembedding's logits (vocabulary). The scalar activation is not used: d = 1 - cos^2 of two non-zero scalars is 0, so every neuron would read r = 1 (appendix, 'Definition questions' 1)
level.In(u): the residual stream feeding the part: a neuron's at its position, before its layer's MLP; a head's at every position up to its own, before its layer's attention; the embedding's the token; the unembedding's the final residual
level.changed part: a part whose cell's weights differ from M's in any entry (exact comparison), or a part M lacks. A part whose cell is unchanged has the same mechanism in both networks, so the swap leaves it alone and it is never a candidate for K (the note, (b): 'a smallest K holds only changed parts')
level.parts F lacks: a neuron whose output column (or a head whose o_proj columns) F has set to zero where M's are not (E195 rebuilt's 8 C neurons, output columns zeroed): absent from F (the note, clause 2); under choice (c5) star absent in every F_K and never in K

readings.main: the note as written. r_u = 1 - mean over v in V_u of d(f_u^F(v), f_u^M(v)), d = 1 - cos^2 of the two writes at the setting v; d(0, 0) = 0, d(0, x) = 1 for x non-zero; a part M lacks r_u = 0. V_u pooled: the settings of In(u) in M's run and in F's run on the item's read windows, every position, each setting weighted equally (2 x n_windows x T settings). F_K by mechanism replacement: every changed part outside K runs M's mechanism on the input it receives in the hybrid; a part M lacks outside K is removed; a part F lacks stays absent (c5 star). K: chunked backward elimination over the changed parts, 5 seeded orders, kept when KL(F || F_K) <= (1 - tau) KL(F || M), tau = closure_bar; rho = mean r_u over K, per order
readings.(i) code's r: on the main K of each order, r_u replaced by E195/E196's aggregate cos^2 (one cos^2 of the part's whole write over every window, position and dimension, M's settings only, the identity pairing: no re-pairing); rho_(i) = its mean over the main K. E196's own number (level A, re-paired, its own K) is quoted from experiments/rule_retention_pairs/results/summary.json beside it, not recomputed
readings.(ii) activation patching (c1): K searched again with F_K made by cross-model activation patching (Prakash et al. 2024): every changed part outside K writes the value it wrote in M's own run on the same window and position; unchanged parts run their shared mechanism on the hybrid's input; a part M lacks outside K writes nothing. r_u as main; rho_(ii) = mean over this K
readings.(iii) M-only settings (c3): on the main K, r_u computed with V_u = M's run only; rho_(iii) its mean
readings.(iv) zeroed parts restored (c5): E195 rebuilt only (the one item with parts F lacks): the 8 C neurons are parts; outside K they run M's mechanism; in K they stay zero and read r = 0 (d(0, x) = 1); K searched again by mechanism replacement; rho_(iv) its mean
readings.(b) size-aware per-setting distance: added 2026-11-18 at the definition lead's request before filing (the user will choose among the code's aggregate (a), this (b) and the note as written (c) from data; no verdict under any): on the main K, r_u = 1 - mean over v in V_u (pooled, as main) of d_b(v), d_b = |f_F - f_M|^2 / (|f_F|^2 + |f_M|^2), 0 when both writes are zero, 1 when one is; a part M lacks r_u = 0; rho_(b) its mean over the main K. A reported number: no rule reads it. In code 'b'; (i) is 'i', (iii) 'iii', main 'main'; each is also averaged over the K of (ii) and (iv)
readings.eps_F: 0 by construction at the identity alignment (the hybrid with nothing swapped is F, read as the gate); not a measurement in this run

rules.R0 (stops): exit 1 with results/stage0_<tag>.json or results/items/<item>.stopped.json 'stopped' on any miss of 'expected' for do_nothing, x2, x10, slotted, neurons_appended, head_appended; and on any item on: the hybrid gate (F part by part with nothing swapped against F's native logits) over gate_tol; the M gate (every changed part, and every part F lacks, swapped, against M's native logits) over m_gate_tol; the identity check (max over neurons with no zero write of |r_main - cos^2 of the output columns|) over identity_tol; an empty K; the E196 gap off E184's by more than reload_tol (code errors, not readings)
rules.R1 (filed, the separating question): for each seed s in {0, 1}: g_pair = mean over the 5 orders of the reuse member's rho_main minus the mean over the 5 orders of the twin's, for the four counted pairs. The seed reads 'A' when g_ident > max(g_repeat, 0) (the identity/random-map gap above the repeat gap and above 0, strictly); 'B' when g_case > g_repeat > max(g_copy, g_ident) (strict: the gaps rank as the twins' update ratios do); 'neither' otherwise, ties included. The two are exclusive (A needs g_ident > g_repeat, B needs g_repeat > g_ident). The filed outcome: 'A' if both seeds read A, 'B' if both read B, else 'mixed'. Reported beside each seed: g_ident - g_repeat and the largest order sd of the four items, so a call within that sd is visible; no band is applied
rules.R1 edge cases: an item whose main contrast reads 'no change' (no changed part) or 'no contrast' (KL(F || M) <= kl_floor) makes its seed 'not read', counted as neither A nor B. K is never empty when F_empty = M (closure of nothing kept is 0 < tau), so an empty K or a None order is a code error and stops. Ties between gaps read 'neither' (strict inequalities in both branches). Zero denominators: KL(F || M) <= kl_floor is 'no contrast' before any division; at a setting where both writes are zero d = 0, where one is zero d = 1. Do-nothing run through R1 as every member gives every g = 0: 'neither' (0 > max(0, 0) and 0 > 0 both fail), so the do-nothing state passes neither rival. All four gaps equal: 'neither'. A reversed repeat pair (g_repeat < 0) with g_ident > 0 reads A; B fails there anyway
rules.R2 (reported, the graft question): rho_main of neurons_appended (0 by the rule) and of slotted beside E206's held-model S for the appended neurons, 0.954 (experiments/graft_sites/results/summary.json); no rule: the appended item is a check, the slotted one a control
rules.R3 (reported, one change at a time): per item and order: rho and |K| under main, (i), (ii), (iii), (b) and, on E195 rebuilt, (iv); per item the differences from main, mean over orders, with the order spread beside them. Expected: (iii) - main = 0 on neuron parts, any difference from heads, embedding and unembedding; (i) - main <= 0 on neuron parts; (ii) and (iv) measured, not predicted

blind_to.r_main at a neuron: everything the neuron responds to: its input row, its norm and any change of gain; it reads only the direction of its output column (algebra above). A neuron with a new input row and the old output column reads r = 1
blind_to.r_main at a head: a change of the head's output size at a setting; it sees a change of where the head attends and of what it writes, because the write's direction varies with the setting
blind_to.rho: how much each part matters: one head weighs as much as one neuron in the mean over K, and K holds thousands of neurons; parts outside the read windows; a change that does not move the behaviour's KL
blind_to.R1: pairs matched in update size (E187's would be the test; not here); the parity twin and fact pair (reported only)

positive_control: stage 0: do-nothing reads 'no change'; x2 and x10 read 1 under every reading; the slotted graft (new parts in M's own slots) reads under slot_bar; the appended grafts read 0 by the rule; F_empty = M on each (the M gate). Same code path, construction and search as the items

noise_floor.rho across orders: E196 level A, largest sd over 5 orders of one item 8.5e-5 (repeat_twin_s0; experiments/rule_retention_pairs/results/summary.json); the main level's own order sd is measured in this run and reported beside R1
noise_floor.gap check: fp32 reload of the same state on the same windows, 0 to about 1e-6 (E196), against reload_tol
